ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
<image>In $\odot G, m \angle A G B=30$ and $\overline{C G} \perp \overline{G D}$.
Find $m \widehat{B C D}$
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended problem

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with G as the center, and A, B, C, D are all on the circle; line segment A-G-D is on the same straight line, so AD is a diameter. The radii GB, GC, GD are also drawn in the figure, and there is a right-angle mark between CG and GD, indicating CG ⟂ GD. The requested m\widehat{BCD} is the measure of the arc from B through C to D. Reasoning: It is known that m∠AGB = 30°. Because CG ⟂ GD, the central angle ∠CGD = 90°. Since A, G, D are collinear and AD is a diameter, ∠AGD is a straight angle, equal to 180°. In this semicircle from ray GA to ray GD, ∠AGB + ∠BGC + ∠CGD = 180°, therefore 30° + ∠BGC + 90° = 180°, solving gives ∠BGC = 60°. A central angle equals the measure of its intercepted arc, so m\widehat{BC} = 60°, m\widehat{CD} = 90°. Therefore m\widehat{BCD} = 60° + 90° = 150°.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: G is the center of the circle, A, B, C, D lie on the circle, and A-G-D is drawn as a straight line, so AD is a diameter. The requested arc \(\widehat{BCD}\) is the minor arc from B to D passing through C. From the text, use \(m\angle AGB=30^\circ\) and \(CG\perp GD\), so \(m\angle CGD=90^\circ\). Since \(\angle AGD\) is a straight central angle, \(m\angle AGD=180^\circ\). Along the upper/right half from ray GA to ray GD, \(\angle AGB+\angle BGC+\angle CGD=180^\circ\), so \(30+\angle BGC+90=180\), giving \(\angle BGC=60^\circ\). Then \(m\widehat{BCD}=m\widehat{BC}+m\widehat{CD}=60+90=150^\circ\).
method.CoT_raw:

推理：已知 m∠AGB = 30°。因为 CG ⟂ GD，所以中心角 ∠CGD = 90°。由于 A、G、D 共线且 AD 为直径，∠AGD 是平角，等于 180°。在从射线 GA 到射线 GD 的这一半圆内，∠AGB + ∠BGC + ∠CGD = 180°，因此 30° + ∠BGC + 90° = 180°，解得 ∠BGC = 60°。中心角等于所对弧的度数，所以 m\widehat{BC} = 60°，m\widehat{CD} = 90°。因此 m\widehat{BCD} = 60° + 90° = 150°。

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: A and D are opposite endpoints of a diameter through center G, and the arc from A to D across the top/right side contains B and C in order. The target \(\widehat{BCD}\) is the portion of that semicircle after removing the small arc \(\widehat{AB}\). From the text, \(m\angle AGB=30^\circ\), so the central angle intercepting arc \(AB\) is \(30^\circ\), hence \(m\widehat{AB}=30^\circ\). Because AD is a diameter, the arc from A to D through B and C is a semicircle of \(180^\circ\). Therefore \(m\widehat{BCD}=180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ\). The perpendicular condition is consistent with C-D contributing a right arc but is not needed once the diameter semicircle and arc AB are used.
